title: The Picture He Built Alone
description:
Three nights. A registry record, a line from an article from back then, one remembered scene at a time.

The name he steered away from — Han PD Construction. The 'Im' who vouched for Park Sang-jin to his father. The man who came up from a Chungcheong fishing town and reached Gangnam by stepping on people.

Three threads met at one point. Im Sangchul.

No one told him. Minjun built the man out of fragments.
And once he knew, the same seat in the same café looked different.

title: A Name That Stayed
description:
At the networking dinner, Sangchul had steered the conversation away from one name: "Han PD Construction."
Minjun filed it away. Weeks passed.

Someone had asked, "What about Han PD Construction?"
Instead of answering, Sangchul had pointed to another table. "Don't mix with that crowd."

1:47 a.m. Sleep would not come, so Minjun searched the name. An old local-news PDF remained online. A guarantee scam from nearly a decade ago. Park Sang-jin. And an unnamed real-estate broker, identified only as Mr. Im, who had connected the victims to him.

The name was redacted. Only a case number remained at the bottom.

Minjun knew the shape of those digits. The paid-in-full certificate he had received after six years of payments carried a number in the same format.

Too specific to dismiss as coincidence. Still one link short of naming a man.

The article said Park Sang-jin had bundled several people's guarantees and diverted the money. A real-estate broker identified as Mr. Im had introduced him to the victims as someone they could trust.

Father had never told Minjun that part. But the certificate Minjun had spent six years earning pointed to the rest of the story.

Minjun's father never spoke the name. Minjun had found it himself.
The man who'd been teaching him to read charts — the same man who back then walked his father into financial ruin.

No one told him. He figured it out alone.
That weight was heavier.

Every time he saw Sangchul now, that name rang somewhere quiet inside him.

He'd pretend not to know. For now.

title: The Question
description:

title: Why Gangnam
description:
Eleven at night.

For the first time, his assets had crossed that number.

Someone asked.
It might have been his father, Hyunsu, or simply a voice carried from somewhere else.

"Why was it Gangnam in the first place?"

After nearly three years of running, {name} had an answer different from the one he would have given at the start.

title: Eleven Minutes Ago
description:
The Seoul-bound KTX had pulled out of Changwon Jungang Station eleven minutes ago.
{name} was returning from an errand in South Gyeongsang that might, eventually, turn into money. Father's hospital had been a fifteen-minute taxi ride from the station. {name} had paused on the platform, then taken his assigned seat for Seoul.

The phone on the tray table shifted a little whenever the train curved. On its screen was a call-log screenshot he had saved years ago.
Father. Twenty-three seconds.

"You doing all right?" "Yeah." "Okay. Hang up, then."
Since moving to Seoul, every call between father and son could be cleared with a few strokes of a thumb. Who had hung up first had blurred. The number had not.

As the train neared a tunnel, {name}'s reflection deepened in the glass. His finger stopped between the screenshot and Father's contact.

choices.text: Open the saved twenty-three-second screenshot
choices.result_text:
{name} enlarged the screenshot. Beneath the contact name were only the time of the call and the number twenty-three.

Rubbing a thumb across the glass brought back none of the words he had failed to say. Instead, the goshiwon ceiling returned, along with Father's breath arriving one beat late through the phone.

choices.text: Close it and find Father's contact
choices.result_text:
He closed the photo app and opened his contacts. Father was only a few swipes down.

It had taken eleven minutes to get from Changwon Jungang Station to this seat. It took less than a second to find the name again.

title: Twenty-Three Seconds
description:
The goshiwon ceiling from that night returned. The lights had been off; only the phone had lit his face. Father was at home in Changwon. {name} was in a one-pyeong room in Seoul.

"You doing all right?"
"Yeah."
"You eating?"
"I am."

A television murmured somewhere behind Father's voice. While Father searched for something more to say, {name} had watched the end-call button. As if having no achievement to report meant having nothing to ask.

"Okay. Hang up, then."

Twenty-three seconds was short. The last silence had been strangely long.

choices.text: Leave the memory and face the number now
choices.result_text:
The train announcement stripped away the goshiwon ceiling. The KTX seat and {name}'s face returned in the window.

Father's contact was still open. So was the call button beneath his name.

title: Call
description:
Father's name sat at the center of the contact screen. Beneath it, the green call button trembled with the train.

{name} tried the first words silently. "Dad, it's me." Obvious words, yet no second sentence came. Was he keeping his hospital appointments? Why hadn't {name} gotten off in Changwon? What, exactly, did he believe he had accomplished in Seoul? Starting anywhere felt like avoiding everything else.

The train entered a tunnel. Hand, face, and call button appeared together in the black window. Saying he would think again after reaching Seoul was not yet a promise made to anyone. Whether to call was an action he could choose only here.

choices.text: Call him
choices.result_text:
{name} pressed the number.

It rang twice. Between the vibration of wheels crossing rail joints came a short breath.

"Yeah. You on the train?"

Father had answered. The call timer began again at one second. The fact of the connection and everything still unsaid remained on the same screen.

choices.text: Do not call
choices.result_text:
{name} moved his hand away from the call button. No new outgoing call appeared. No missed call had come in from Father either. What remained was the fact that Minjun had opened the number and chosen not to press.

The thought that he would call after reaching Seoul still sounded plausible. The screen went dark on its own, and his face appeared in the black glass. The train moved farther from Changwon.

title: Leaving the Name Blank
description:
At 6:38 Wednesday evening, {name} opened Father's old guarantee PDF beside Jaehyuk's application and the search result for Han PD Construction. The signature boxes looked alike; the Mapo dates and addresses were close. But the article identified the introducer only as Mr. Im, and the court and bank fields he had tried to verify still held no full name.

Sangchul's old office had been nearby. Nearby was not proof. One extra letter would turn inference into accusation.

Sangchul's chat was still empty. Seven tomorrow evening was open on the calendar. {name}'s task was not to name a culprit. It was to state, once, what he had verified, what remained blank, and when he would ask in person.

choices.text: Send verified facts and blanks separately, then give him the seven o'clock meeting time
choices.result_text:
{name} split the message into two paragraphs.

‘The signature boxes in the guarantee and application look alike, and the Mapo dates and addresses are close. I have not verified the introducer's full name or a link between the cases. I will ask you in person tomorrow at seven.’

Sent at 6:46. He attached no copies. Sangchul had a night to prepare, but the chat gave equal weight to what {name} knew and what he did not.

choices.result_text:

‘Were you the introducer named in this record? Please answer only yes or no. I will bring the current copies tomorrow at seven.’

The screens could not be taken back. They created a common record that would be harder to deny later, but also gave Sangchul time to study every page and every place {name} had covered.

choices.text: Send no evidence, only the blank and the meeting time
choices.result_text:
‘There is one introducer's name I could not verify. I will bring the current records and ask you in person tomorrow at seven.’

{name} sent only those two sentences. Neither Sangchul's name nor a case number entered the chat. He kept the pages from leaving his hands, but a notice with no explanation sounded closer to a warning than a question.

The brown envelope and sent time remained. The chat held none of the reason behind the question.

title: Twenty-Three Seconds Toward Seoul
description:
The Seoul-bound KTX had emerged from its first tunnel after leaving Changwon Jungang Station. The water bottle on the tray trembled at every rail joint. Father's call had been connected for twenty-three seconds.

"You on the train?"
"Yes. I'm heading up to Seoul."

A carriage announcement filled the pause. From Father's end came cloth shifting and a short breath. The fact that {name} had passed a station fifteen minutes by taxi from the hospital and taken his assigned seat for Seoul did not disappear because the call connected.

"Say it if you have something to say," Father said. "I'm listening." The call kept running, but {name} could give only one thing the whole of his attention.

choices.text: Ask how Father's body feels now, and do not interrupt before the answer ends
choices.result_text:
"What hurts most right now?"

Father did not answer at once. As the next tunnel came into view, he said, "A little short of breath today." {name} did not say it was fine or tell him what to do.

Listening to one answer left no room for the explanation {name} had prepared. In return, he heard exactly where Father's breathing shortened.

choices.text: Admit that he took the Seoul train without getting off near the hospital
choices.result_text:
"I knew the hospital was close and still didn't get off. I stayed on the train to Seoul."

Something rang softly against Father's bed rail. After a long pause, he said only, "All right." Forgiveness or acknowledgment—{name} could not tell.

{name} did not explain how important the errand in South Gyeongsang had been. The Seoul arrival time did not change, but the face he could have saved until then was already gone.

choices.text: Give the Seoul arrival time to the exact minute and do not hide where he is
choices.result_text:
"I arrive at Seoul Station at 8:12. Right now I'm moving farther from Changwon."

Father repeated, "Eight twelve," slowly. A number describing the present route, not a feeling, became the clearest thing on the call screen.

{name} left Father's condition and the hospital visit unspoken. He did not hide where he was going. That precision did not reduce the distance created by not being there.

title: The Number He Did Not Dial
description:
The Seoul-bound KTX emerged from its first tunnel after leaving Changwon Jungang Station. {name} kept Father's contact open and moved his hand away from the call button. No new outgoing call appeared. No missed call had come in from Father either.

His photos still held the screen from a twenty-three-second call years ago. The train app showed the Changwon departure and expected Seoul arrival. His notes held half a sentence to Father. None could turn the call he had not made into a conversation.

choices.text: Finish the line to Father, but do not send it
choices.result_text:
{name} completed the line: "Dad, I'm on a train from Changwon to Seoul. I opened your number and did not call." He added the time, then kept the send window closed.

The sentence was complete but did not reach Father. The original remained, preventing him from later claiming that he had sent it.

The fastest ticket from Seoul could put him inside the room tonight. If he called the ward now, a nurse could try to connect the phone to Father. If he could do neither, he would have to leave a reply under his own name saying that he was postponing the contact.

The train app, ward number, and read receipt shared one screen. {name} chose an action he would take now, not the outcome of the crisis.

title: Counting the Same Breath
description:
The hospital window was open the width of a palm. Late rain and antiseptic met above the bed. {name} had actually reached the room and pulled up a chair. Tape marks crossed Father's hand, and the fingers outside the blanket looked thinner than they had when he worked at the factory.

"You came."
"Yes."

Father asked nothing else. Arriving did not erase the time before it or decide what came next. Beside the bed were only a hand whose permission could still be asked, one sentence left unsaid when they spoke of the guarantee, and breathing that would not keep a schedule.

{name} sat at the edge of the chair, close enough for Father to notice whatever he chose.

choices.text: Ask Father for permission before holding his hand
choices.result_text:
"Can I hold your hand?"

Father opened his eyes, looked once at {name}, and turned his hand slightly. {name} rested his palm on only the space offered. He did not call it cold or tighten his grip.

The prepared sentence went unsaid while he asked permission. What remained was Father's present answer: he did not pull his fingers away.

choices.text: Say the one honest sentence he withheld when Father signed the guarantee
choices.result_text:
"When you signed the guarantee, I knew something was wrong and pretended I didn't."

Father's gaze lowered slowly from the ceiling. "Don't come now and say you'll settle it all with money."

That sentence closed the path to ending this as a number. {name} could not continue his explanation. He had to receive Father's answer without revising it.

choices.text: Add no words and count Father's breaths with him
choices.result_text:
{name} folded his fingers over his knee. One, two, three. The seventh breath came late; the eighth ran long.

"What are you counting?"
"I'm just here."

He did not explain. His questions and the guarantee remained untouched, but for those few minutes he did not force Father's breathing to match his schedule.

title: One Connected Sentence
description:
The call was connected. {name} stood at the window, holding the phone in both hands. Beyond Father's voice came the wheels of a hospital cart, then a short breath. The call timer grew; the distance to Changwon did not shrink.

"Minjun."
"Yes, Dad."

{name} had three things available: admitting that he had decided on the hospital visit alone, stating that he could not arrive today, or leaving his explanations aside and hearing one sentence of Father's to the end. He could do all three without hanging up, but then he would fill the time with his own voice again.

While Father gathered breath, {name} chose one.

choices.text: Admit that he decided alone whether to make or postpone the hospital visit
choices.result_text:
"I decided alone whether to go to the hospital or postpone it. I didn't ask you."

Father did not answer immediately. Only after the cart wheels receded did he say, "Yes. You did."

{name} added no explanation. The call continued, but the old choice could no longer be covered by saying he had been busy.

choices.text: State plainly that he cannot reach Changwon today
choices.result_text:
"I can't reach Changwon today. I'm still in Seoul."

Father said, very quietly, "I understand." {name} did not cover it with a new promise.

The truth removed any false arrival time Father might wait for. It also turned the distance between them from a number into Father's brief answer.

choices.text: Offer no defense and hear one sentence Father chooses to the end
choices.result_text:
{name} said only, "Go ahead."

After taking two breaths, Father said, "Don't hang up today. Stay a while."

{name} asked nothing and explained nothing. His prepared words moved aside as the call timer grew. One sentence Father had chosen remained unbroken between them.

title: The Time He Postponed Contact
description:
The phone held the time the ward first contacted {name} and the separate time he replied, "I can't today." There was no outgoing call to Father and no missed call from him. {name} had neither left for Changwon nor asked the ward for a connection.

The ward's next message said, "The patient is not available for calls at present." Nothing beyond that sentence had been confirmed. In the notes app, a line beginning "Dad" stopped halfway through a word.

{name} possessed the ward's contact time, the time he postponed it, and one sentence never sent. He would copy one into his notebook so a better excuse could not replace it later.

In preserving the exact times, he left the voice and words he might have heard blank. The space did not shrink when he lifted the pen.

{name} copied the message through its final period. He wrote neither critical nor fine.

He invented no outcome beyond what was known, but Father's voice was replaced by an institution's sentence. On the page, a person narrowed into one status line.

choices.text: Finish the unsent sentence, but do not send it

{name} finished the line: "Dad, I received the contact today and still chose to postpone it myself." He added the time and moved his hand away from send.

The sentence was complete but did not reach Father. What {name} had meant to say remained. The place for a response from the person who might hear it was blank for now.

title: Until the Next Test
description:
The ward called again. After oxygen support and a medication adjustment, Father's acute respiratory deterioration had stopped getting worse. The doctor used the word stable, not discharge. The chronic illness remained, and Father would stay admitted for the next test and continued observation.

The nurse read out the current medications, the next oxygen check, and the next test time. Surviving one crisis had not finished the work of care. {name} still had to decide who would confirm what from this point forward.

choices.text: Read back the medications, oxygen-check time, and next test, then take the guardian contact
choices.result_text:
{name} read back each medication name and administration time, the oxygen-check time, and the next test. The nurse corrected one time, and Minjun's number remained first on the guardian contact list.

No sentence said that Father was cured. What had been settled was who would answer the next call and what he would ask. Minjun left the list open and set the first alarm.

choices.text: Cancel work through the next test and make time in which he cannot miss the ward's call
choices.result_text:
{name} canceled what overlapped the next test. One confirmed payment disappeared from his ledger. He told the other party only that he needed to receive a family ward call, adding neither the diagnosis nor a claim that Father was better.

He disabled silent mode and exempted the ward number. The acute deterioration had stopped, but admission and chronic illness continued. The time he cleared was not a reward for a cure. It was space in which not to miss the next change.

title: An Unconfirmed Course
description:
The ward connection ended during a staff handoff. The next notice contained only an intake time and an expected callback time. The records currently available could not establish whether Father had survived the acute deterioration or had not.

{name} did not fill the blank with hope or bereavement. He kept only the ward number, the patient's name, and the time at which someone would call again on one screen. Until the next confirmation, those were all the facts he could state.

choices.text: Keep only the confirmed times and ward number, and do not declare an outcome
choices.result_text:
{name} copied the intake and expected callback times exactly. He wrote neither stable nor dead. No guess entered the record in place of Father's present condition.

When he closed the screen, two times without an outcome remained in the notebook. Enduring what he did not know was different from inventing an ending that was not there.

title: The Night the Guarantee PDF Arrived
description:
Jaehyuk's long-silent chat rose to the top with one file notification. Its preview held the title GUARANTEE REQUEST, a debtor field, and an empty guarantor signature line on the same screen. A short message sat beneath the file.

“Minjun, look at this before we talk. I'll tell you all of why I came back to you now.”

{name} did not open the signing screen. He wrote no refusal either. The immediate task was not to answer the request, but to preserve the words and time in which it had arrived. Sangchul's seven-page offer and the identical copy sent to Daeun already sat beside each other in Downloads. This PDF needed its own locked folder, merged with neither. The message box remained empty while the attachment icon stayed blue.

texts: Downloads held the same filename sent first to Sangchul and two minutes later to Daeun. One copy carried the note that proposer and reviewer were the same person; the other said the name page had not been removed. The new guarantee request could not be recorded apart from its recipient and original either.

choices.text: Move the original request and PDF into a separate folder and preserve their arrival time
choices.result_text:
{name} placed Jaehyuk's message and attachment in the same locked folder. He added only the received date and time to the filename, no verdict such as safe or fraud.

Inside the folder, the request sat above the empty signature line. No message bubble of his own appeared in the chat. When he closed the screen, the download bar vanished and one lock symbol remained beside the new PDF.

title: The Call About Why He Returned
description:
The call {name} placed connected on the third ring. Traffic and a hastily swallowed breath overlapped on Jaehyuk's end.

“I did run. I was one of the people trapped at first. But the debt stayed under my name, and the old crowd started avoiding my calls. I thought if I finished this document, I could start again. That's why I thought of you.”

Jaehyuk carried his mixture of excuse and circumstance to the end. {name} did not interrupt. Beneath the call screen, the archived PDF remained open. Its debtor field, separate lines for the total and guarantee limit, and the first message using a friend's name each raised a different question. Asking all three at once would leave none heard through. {name} chose the first question he would finish.

texts: The locked folder held Jaehyuk's original request, its received time, and the still-empty guarantor signature line together. No reply bubble from {name} existed, making this call the first direct act toward the request he had preserved.

choices.text: Ask first for the name in the debtor field and Jaehyuk's relationship to it
choices.result_text:
“What is your relationship to the name in the debtor field?”

Jaehyuk read the corporate name once, then stopped. “I'm not listed as the borrower. My name is tied to the guarantee side too.”

{name} wrote his explanation beside the field. He did not reach the total or why Jaehyuk had chosen him. When the call fell quiet, the long name in the debtor box seemed darker on the screen.

choices.text: Have him read where the total and the guarantee liability part ways
choices.result_text:
“Not the total. Read exactly what you would be liable for.”

Jaehyuk first said the figures were the same, then reopened the PDF. After a pause, he read the total and the guarantee cap separately. The two lines did not end in the same place.

{name} marked their different endings. The debtor relationship and the reason for choosing a friend's name stayed beyond this question. Only the sound of Jaehyuk turning pages moved between the figures.

choices.text: Ask why he chose a friend's name instead of anyone else's
choices.result_text:
“Why me? Not the document—the reason you chose my name.”

Jaehyuk gave a short laugh and stopped. “In the army, you were the one who stayed to the end. Even after I went under, your name still felt like it did then.”

Friend was both an answer and material for the request. {name} copied the sentence into the call note. The debtor and guarantee-limit questions remained open, but his own name looked heavier on the screen.

title: The Same Fields on Two Documents
description:
Jaehyuk's PDF remained open after the call. {name} took the copy of Father's old guarantee document from his private files. One was a gray scan of paper long kept folded; the other was a white PDF received today.

Their eras and typefaces differed. Yet both placed a guarantor's name after the debtor and pushed the fine print defining liability onto the next page. Father's document carried a signature that had long since set. The line waiting for him on Jaehyuk's file was still empty.

{name} did not merge the files. An old failure would not decide today's request for him. Instead, he would align only the name fields and liability clauses so that what matched—and what remained blank—could be seen at once.

texts: The call note placed the debtor's corporate name, Jaehyuk's relationship to it, and his admission that his own name sat on the guarantee side beside the debtor field. {name} aligned that field first with the debtor-and-guarantor order in Father's document.
The call note marked the total and guarantee-cap lines ending at different places. {name} found the separate ends of total and liability in Father's document and set them at the same height.
The call note preserved Jaehyuk's reason for choosing a friend's name verbatim beside the PDF. {name} opened a separate comparison so that sentence could not stand in for the guarantor field.

choices.text: Align the name fields and liability clauses in a separate comparison copy
choices.result_text:
{name} set the guarantor field on Father's document level with the empty signature line in Jaehyuk's PDF. On the next screen he marked only where each liability clause began and ended.

He added neither conclusion nor arrow. Father's settled name remained on the left; his own empty field remained on the right. The cursor blinked once between them and stopped.

title: The Guarantee Request Before Daeun
description:
Across the laptop, Daeun read Jaehyuk's original request, the verified guarantee scope, and the comparison with Father's document. None of the files carried {name}'s signature yet.

“Mr. Minjun, you didn't call me just to leave proof that you showed me, did you?”

{name} kept all three screens open. He still had to choose what to move forward first. Starting with money pushed aside who had made the request and why. Starting with names exposed Jaehyuk's and Father's circumstances to Daeun. Starting with the arrival time meant accounting for the hours he had held the file alone before discussing the paper.

Daeun did not choose for him. She withdrew her hand from the laptop. “Show me what you most want to hide first. Then I can read the rest with my own eyes.”

texts: The separate comparison aligned Father's settled name, Jaehyuk's empty field, and only the beginnings and ends of both liability clauses. With neither conclusion nor arrow added, Daeun could ask what judgment the arrangement itself concealed.

choices.text: Open with the total and guarantee scope, showing the size of the money first
choices.result_text:
{name} enlarged the total and the line where guarantee liability ended. Daeun read both figures, then placed one finger in the gap between them.

“Did Jaehyuk tell you this difference, or did it appear only after you asked?”

{name} distinguished what Jaehyuk had volunteered from the line verified directly in the PDF. The shape of the money was clear. The reason for choosing a friend's name and the time he had kept the file alone remained on the screens behind it. Daeun did not look away from the figures.

choices.text: Open with Jaehyuk's and Father's name fields and show the repeated structure
choices.result_text:
{name} brought the comparison forward. Daeun looked from Father's name on the left to the empty field on the right, then read the original request in which Jaehyuk had called him by name.

“If you stop at saying they look alike, the people become fields again. Your name is still blank, correct?”

{name} showed her the blank. Two men's circumstances were now exposed; the numerical difference and the hours he had held the file remained behind them.

choices.text: Disclose first the time between the file's arrival and showing it to Daeun
choices.result_text:
{name} read the received time, the call time, and the time he opened the file before Daeun. He stated without defense why he had held it alone between those moments.

Daeun did not immediately say it was all right. “Was my name beside this request during those hours too?”

{name} reopened all three screens. The withheld time was exposed, but judgment over the amount and names had not been handed to Daeun. Three timestamps and one empty signature line remained in the room.

title: The Act Left in the Guarantee Field
description:
Three actions remained open: Jaehyuk's message box, the e-signature button on the guarantee PDF, and Block in the contact menu. The time Daeun saw the request and the comparison with Father's document stayed beside them.

Jaehyuk's last sentence on the call was brief. “Minjun, decide. Just don't pretend you never saw it.”

Refusal would leave the signature blank and the channel open. Signing would put his name and authentication time in the empty field—and immediately record that he had crossed Father's line. Blocking would send a boundary against further contact about this request, then close the channel. None determined Jaehyuk's response or the guarantee's future. What could move now was a sentence, a signature, or the block control.

texts: Daeun had placed one finger between the total and guarantee scope, asking whether their difference came from Jaehyuk or only after {name}'s question. Before touching e-signature, {name} reread the record where he separated those two sources.
After seeing Father's settled name beside Jaehyuk's empty field, Daeun had asked whether {name}'s name was still blank. E-signature would answer her with irreversible black letters.

When {name} read the received time, call time, and disclosure time, Daeun asked whether her name had sat beside the request during those hours. Those three times and her question would remain even if he pressed Block.

choices.text: Send Jaehyuk a refusal to guarantee while leaving the contact channel open
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote, ‘I will not sign this guarantee. Do not put my name on this document,’ and sent it. The signature line remained blank, and the conversation stayed open.

Only a sent time appeared beneath his bubble. The place for Jaehyuk's response remained as it was, but the refusal could no longer be mistaken for silence. The call button remained at one edge of the screen; the signature button went untouched.

choices.text: Enter his name in the electronic-signature field and complete authentication
choices.result_text:
{name} read the guarantee scope once more from top to bottom, then entered his name in the electronic-signature field. When authentication finished, black letters filled the blank and the signing time appeared automatically.

He sent no new sentence in Jaehyuk's chat. The screen held only the completed-authentication mark, the liability scope, and his name. The field that had let light through before Daeun no longer did.

choices.text: Tell Jaehyuk not to contact him again about this guarantee, then block him
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote, ‘Do not contact me again about this document or guarantee request.’ After the sent time appeared, he selected Block in the contact menu.

The chat preserved every earlier word while closing its input. The PDF signature line stayed blank, and the call button disappeared. A short block notice appeared at the bottom; Jaehyuk's familiar voice and request remained above it.

title: A Sentence That Reaches Jaehyuk—or Only Himself
description:
A few days later, {name} opened the Jaehyuk guarantee decision beside the non-transfer notice sent to Sangchul. The fact that no money moved on the property side did not change what actually remained from the guarantee: a blank signature, a completed electronic signature, or a closed conversation.

{name} could write one sentence aimed at Jaehyuk in the place left by that earlier decision, or touch no channel and keep both outcomes only in his own ledger. Either way, the guarantee state already on record would remain.

texts: The conversation remained open after {name} refused the guarantee. A sentence written in this choice will be sent to Jaehyuk through that input.

Jaehyuk's conversation remained open after {name} completed the electronic signature. A sentence written in this choice will be sent through that input, while the name and authentication time remain on the PDF.

The input and call button remained closed after {name} blocked Jaehyuk. A sentence written in this choice will not reach Jaehyuk; it will remain under UNDELIVERED—CHANNEL BLOCKED in the personal ledger.
The notice to Sangchul held one sentence saying the current papers had not reached execution and no transfer was made, beside its sent time.

choices.text: Leave one sentence about the non-transfer result in the place the earlier decision left open
choices.result_text: In the one place left by that earlier decision, {name} wrote, ‘There was no contract to execute on the property side, so no money moved. My decision on your guarantee remains unchanged,’ and kept the time. He neither reopened a closed channel nor changed the signature field, whether blank or filled.

choices.text: Touch no Jaehyuk channel and keep both outcomes only in his own ledger
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the actual guarantee state and the sent time of the non-transfer notice on separate lines. Between them he wrote, ONE OUTCOME DOES NOT ERASE THE OTHER.

He did not open Jaehyuk's conversation. Only today's time was added to the personal ledger; no sentence aimed at Jaehyuk remained.

title: Reaching Out to Daeun First
description:
A few minutes after the last signature, {name} closed the notebook and opened the conversation where he and Daeun had actually exchanged words. Whoever held the comparison, the screen contained only the sentences and times they had sent, with an empty input below.

Instead of the KRW 3 billion figure or a photograph of a key, he could send one action from his side: a date and place for a meal next week, an apology for calculating with Daeun's name before waiting for her answer, or the distance he needed tonight and the time he would contact her again. What happened after sending would remain on the other side of the screen.

texts: The delivery time on the comparison Daeun had taken home returned beside the older messages in the conversation.
NOT DELIVERED was already in the notebook before {name} opened the conversation.
Moments ago, {name} gathered what he had begun and stopped into one sentence beneath his own name. An act outside that sentence remained.
Moments ago, {name} put each person's time and the weight of each name into the cost column. The message to Daeun had to be chosen outside that ledger.
Moments ago, {name} wrote other people's names first and his own at the end. Now he had to call one of those names again in an actual conversation.

choices.text: Propose a date and place for a meal next week
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote, ‘Next Sunday at seven, I'd like to eat with you near the convenience store where we first exchanged names. Tell me later if another day is better.’

The screen remained empty below the sent time. Inside his own bubble, a date and place had taken the shape of an invitation.

choices.text: Apologize for calculating with Daeun's name before waiting for her answer
choices.result_text: {name} wrote, ‘I calculated the place your name could occupy before I waited for your answer. I'm sorry. I won't press you for a reply.’ He sent the sentence without shortening it, and a sent time appeared beneath the apology.

choices.text: Send the distance he needs tonight and the time he will contact her again
choices.result_text:
{name} sent, ‘I want to close the papers and be alone tonight. I'll contact you first tomorrow at eight.’ He placed the next act and time after the request for distance.

Before he turned the phone over, only the sent time sat beneath his bubble. The duty to return at eight remained on this side of the screen.

title: Reaching Out to Jiyeon First
description:
At 12:11 a.m. Tuesday of the final week, {name} set the key envelope and execution copy on his desk, then opened the conversation he had shared with Jiyeon. The screen held only their earlier words.

What Jiyeon had said before the broker returned: ‘On the next document, don't make my place before waiting for my answer.’ Her voice returned in {name}'s handwriting in the execution copy's margin.

The time {name} had postponed answering stretched above the input box. He touched it without posting the goal figure or a key photograph. Rather than wait for Jiyeon to decide the relationship, he would send one present act: a meal, an overdue apology, or the distance he needed and his next contact time.

choices.text: Propose a date and place for dinner next week
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote, ‘I would like to have dinner with you next Sunday at seven, near the office where we first opened the papers. Please tell me later if another day is better.’

He added nothing about reaching the goal or sharing the key. When he sent it, 12:16 appeared beneath his bubble. He had offered one concrete table; the apology he had postponed remained outside the message box.

choices.text: Apologize first for waiting on her answer only after calculating with her name
choices.result_text:
‘I calculated the place your name could occupy before I waited for your answer. I am sorry. This apology is not a demand for a reply.’

{name} sent the sentence without shortening it. No read mark or new bubble appeared. Beside the execution copy, the apology gained a real time, while where they might meet next week remained unset.

choices.text: Send the distance he needs tonight and the time he will contact her again
choices.result_text:
{name} sent, ‘I want to read this executed copy alone again tonight. I will call you first tomorrow at eight thirty.’ He placed the time of his own action after the request for distance.

Just before he turned the phone over, only the sent time remained beneath his own bubble. Metal shifted inside the key envelope when the phone went face down. Tonight's silence and the next contact time sat inside the same bubble.

title: Reaching Out to Hyunsu First
description:
After leaving Hyunsu, {name} spread his self-filed copy, non-execution notice, and seven pages to return across the floor. A round mark from the cafe water glass occupied the place where a key might have been.

Hyunsu's voice from the cafe returned over the water ring. ‘Hyung, not using a person as collateral doesn't erase how long people waited.’ At the bottom of their conversation were dates and times they had exchanged; {name}'s input box was blank.

He searched for their old goshiwon soup place, then erased the name. Rather than call non-execution victory or defeat, he could offer a specific meal, send a late apology, or state the distance he needed and his next call time. He would not wait for Hyunsu to ask again.

choices.text: Send a date and time for the soup place near the old goshiwon
choices.result_text:
{name} sent, ‘This Saturday at one, let's eat at that soup place near the goshiwon. I'll be there first.’

He did not add a long explanation for leaving the contract unexecuted. Only the sent time appeared; the space below remained blank. He had offered an actual seat over a bowl of soup, while how long he had made Hyunsu wait remained unsaid.

choices.text: Apologize first for hearing Hyunsu's words too late
choices.result_text:
‘When you told me to see the time people spent without becoming collateral, I should have answered. I'm sorry I erased the waiting like a number.’

{name} added that the apology was late and sent it. Only a sent time appeared beneath the bubble. The apology gained a time distinct from the non-execution notice, but it did not manufacture a place where they would meet next.

choices.text: Send the distance he needs tonight and the time he will call again
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote, ‘I want to close the papers and be alone tonight. I'll call you first tomorrow at eight.’ He did not ask Hyunsu to understand.

After sending it, he turned the phone over. The seven pages still to return remained on the floor. Before the screen went dark, one next time remained in his own message bubble.

title: The Call to a Junior's Sister
description:
At 5:42 p.m. on his first Friday as lead, the partner company still had not sent the answer needed for next week's launch. A junior raised his phone. His sister worked there; one question after her shift could keep Monday on schedule. The team lead told {name} to decide.

Hyunsu arrived outside the office. {name} had asked to meet face-to-face after work. Hearing the situation through the open door, he spoke to {name}, not the junior. “Hyung, whose work is making him call his sister?”

Blocking the call would cost the schedule and first evaluation. Allowing it would spend the sister's standing at work. Returning authority to the team lead could protect both names but end the role in its first week. Hyunsu did not choose for him.

choices.text: Send the junior home, block the call, and carry the weekend until the official answer arrives
choices.result_text:
{name} told the junior to put away the phone and go home. He told the team lead to delay Monday and leave both possible plans to him for the weekend. The team lead said the reason for the delay would remain in his first-week evaluation.

Hyunsu did not suggest leaving together. “This time you spent your weekend instead of someone else's family. Next time, stop it inside company time.” He entered the elevator alone. In the empty office, {name} began with the names of the people he would have to apologize to Monday. The role remained; his first weekend and the quick success did not.

choices.text: Have the junior get his sister's answer and keep Monday on schedule
choices.result_text:
The junior stepped into the hallway and called his sister. He returned with the needed answer but did not look up. “She said not to contact her about company work again.” The team lead confirmed Monday's launch, and {name}'s first-week result survived.

Hyunsu never entered the meeting room. Passing {name}, he said only, “The name changed, hyung.” After the elevator closed, the junior placed his phone facedown on the desk. The schedule had opened. The path for that employee to mention his family at work had closed.

choices.text: Refuse authority that begins with a call to someone's family and return it to the team lead
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the new access card before the team lead. “If this call is the first decision of the role, I won't hold the authority.” The team lead sent the junior home and agreed to wait for the official answer. He also made clear that the appointment and recommendation ended here.

Hyunsu walked only as far as the crosswalk. He offered no praise. “Don't say you stepped down for me. It was work you said you couldn't do.” When the light changed, they crossed in different directions. The junior's family and the weekend remained protected. The door meant to open for {name} on Monday closed inside the company.

title: The Last Screw on the First Monday
description:
On acquisition's first Monday, one screw remained below the new logo. Friday held three commitments: the team's last independent dinner, the night at Sujin’s workplace, and the first post-acquisition transition gathering. {name} kept one and missed two. Paper cups left by the team sat stacked in the dark meeting room. Sujin's message remained: “Someone answered Friday. Who do I call next Monday?”

A ribbon brought by the buyer marked the transition seat. The acquisition lead paused. “Whichever seat you chose, don't repay the other two by rushing people today.” The cofounder, who had stayed through the first Monday, crouched at the door and took out a screwdriver. “We know where you were. The other places don't disappear.” Before the team arrived, one screw remained among those traces.

choices.text: Before the team arrives, remove the old sign's last screw with the cofounder
choices.result_text:
{name} knelt beside the cofounder and held the sign's corner. Each time the cofounder turned the screwdriver half a turn, {name} steadied it. When the last screw came free, they lowered the old sign to the floor.

The elevator stopped, and the team's voices drew closer down the hall. A bare hole showed beneath the new logo, while Sujin's question remained paused at the end of the playback bar. The cofounder placed the screw on an open palm. They stood and faced the first Monday's door together.
